master_output.idea:
To enhance the performance of the model within the constraint of 10 training epochs, one approach could involve leveraging knowledge distillation. Knowledge distillation is a technique where a smaller model (student) is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, more complex model (teacher). This can often lead to better performance due to the student model learning from the richer representation space of the teacher.

In this context, we can pre-train a large model (teacher) on the same dataset for a longer period or with more data. Once the teacher model is well-trained, we use it to generate predictions for the training set. These predictions can then be used as soft targets for training the actual model defined in `train.py` (the student). The student model would aim to minimize the difference between its predictions and those of the teacher, typically using a loss function that incorporates both the hard labels and the soft targets generated by the teacher.

This approach allows the student model to benefit from the knowledge acquired by the teacher without needing extensive training time, thus fitting well within the 10-epoch constraint while potentially achieving higher performance.

Core idea: Use knowledge distillation to train the model with soft targets generated by a pre-trained teacher model.
Non-trivial crux: Designing an effective loss function that balances the importance of the original hard labels and the soft targets provided by the teacher model.
